Combine pipeline steps into a list of steps

Source: R/run_step.R
c.condathis_run_step.Rd

c() on classed lists splices their fields into one list and drops the class. For steps it returns a list of steps instead, of class condathis_run_steps, so run_pipeline(!!!c(step_1, step_2)) works. Its own c() method keeps it that way: c(c(step_1, step_2), step_3), c(step_1, c(step_2, step_3)) and Reduce(c, steps) give one flat list of steps. Plain lists of steps are flattened into the result, and NULL values are dropped, as by c(), so c(step_1, if (gz) step_2) works.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'condathis_run_step'
c(...)

# S3 method for class 'condathis_run_steps'
c(...)

# S3 method for class 'condathis_run_steps'
x[i]

# S3 method for class 'condathis_run_steps'
as.list(x, ...)

Arguments

...

condathis_run_step objects, lists of them, NULL, or other values.

x

A condathis_run_steps object.

i

Index of the steps to keep.

Value

A condathis_run_steps object (a list of condathis_run_step objects) when every value is a step, a list of steps or NULL. Otherwise the plain list that the default c() gives, with the steps as elements. [ keeps the class, and as.list() removes it.

Details

Any other value gives a plain list, as the default c() does, and run_pipeline() reports the values that are not steps. So do.call(run_pipeline, c(steps, list(verbose = "silent"))) works.

c() dispatches on its first argument only: c(steps, step) with a plain list or NULL as steps uses the default method and splits step into its fields. Write c(steps, list(step)) there, or start from a step.
